title: Spicy Sesame Cold Noodles
summary: Thin wheat noodles rinsed cold and tossed in a sweet, tangy gochujang sauce with crisp cucumber. A summer lunch that comes together in fifteen minutes.

creator.bio: Sample creator. Korean home cooking the way my mom taught me: stews, banchan and noodles for busy nights.

ingredients.name: somen noodles
ingredients.notes: thin wheat noodles; any thin noodle works

steps.instruction: Stir the gochujang, rice vinegar, sugar, soy sauce and sesame oil together in a large bowl until smooth.
success_cues: Sauce is smooth and glossy with no sugar grit at the bottom
steps.creator_note: Taste it now. It should be a bit too strong on its own; the noodles calm it down.

steps.instruction: Cut the cucumber into thin matchsticks.
success_cues: Matchsticks are thin and roughly even
warnings: Sharp knife: curl your fingertips under and keep the board steady on a damp towel.

steps.instruction: Boil the noodles according to the package, usually 2 to 3 minutes, stirring so they don't clump.
success_cues: Noodles are tender all the way through with no hard core
warnings: Boiling water: pour away from you and use oven mitts on the pot handles.

steps.instruction: Drain the noodles and rinse under cold running water, rubbing them with your hands, until they feel cold and no longer starchy. Shake off as much water as you can.
success_cues: Noodles feel cold and smooth, not sticky
No water dripping from the colander
warnings: Pour the boiling water away from you into the sink.

steps.instruction: Toss the noodles in the sauce, pile into bowls and top with cucumber, the egg half and sesame seeds if using.

creator_notes: Leave out the egg and it is vegan.
dietary_warnings: Contains wheat (noodles, gochujang, soy sauce), soy and sesame. Optional egg.
